populations.resultSummary: control 159/256; treatment 159/256; 0 gains/0 losses; aggregate workSpent BYTE-IDENTICAL (29,676,406,171 both arms) -- not a normal clean null (contrast confirm-broad-002's nonzero +0.01% work delta despite 0/0). Diagnosed as repair-fallback saturation: isMustCrossFlipperHeavy's gate is a strict superset of needsRepairFallback's gate, so every eligible level also gets an early repair probe before this candidate's new main-loop configs could ever run; a fresh uniform-random cohort's eligible levels are overwhelmingly repair-resistant-negative (repair solves them) unlike the development population, which was mined specifically from levels the whole existing ladder (repair included) already fails on. See reports/2026-08-26-mustcross-flipper-wide-beam-exposure-development-ab.md's 'Confirmation attempt' section. Not evidence of no mechanism -- do not promote or close negative on this run.

P(zero participating rows | n=1200, p=0.0176) ~= 7e-10, ruling out chance; a local sanity check directly on the 3 known development-positive levels (R00817/R02010/R02151) reproduced the original +3/-0 result exactly, confirming the mechanism is real and not a wiring bug -- freshly generated uniform-random cohorts evidently cannot exercise this candidate at any feasible count. See reports/2026-08-26-mustcross-flipper-wide-beam-exposure-development-ab.md's 'Confirmation attempts' section. Not evidence of no mechanism -- do not promote or close negative on this run; escalate to the two-phase control-failure-residual design (confirm-residual-001) instead of scaling count further.

populations.phase1Description: Generate a fresh 1,200-level pool (master seed 2026082701, id prefix J -- never used by a prior cohort) and run the CONTROL ladder alone across it at the same node_budget=50000000 envelope. Freeze the subset it fails to solve as the phase-2 residual corpus. This mirrors exactly how the original 724-level Corpus-2 residual population was defined (mining current production misses), applied to a fresh generated pool instead of the existing corpus.
populations.phase2Description: Run BOTH control and treatment (enable_flags=STRATEGY_MUSTCROSS_FLIPPER_WIDE_BEAM_EXPOSURE) on the frozen phase-1 residual corpus only, same node_budget=50000000 envelope. The residual's exact size and level set are determined by phase 1's outcome and cannot be known before phase 1 completes -- this entry reserves the identity/seed, not a fixed level set.
populations.selectionRule: Phase-1 filtering is by whether CONTROL alone solves a fresh level, decided before either arm's real phase-2 comparison ever runs -- a pre-outcome-neutral selection rule, not selection by whether treatment succeeds. Once phase 1's residual composition has informed this decision it cannot be reused for a different candidate.
populations.materializationTool: .github/workflows/solver-residual-confirmation.yml (dispatched with cohort_id=confirm-residual-001, master_seed=2026082701, id_prefix=J, pool_count=1200, enable_flags=STRATEGY_MUSTCROSS_FLIPPER_WIDE_BEAM_EXPOSURE, node_budget=50000000)
populations.resultSummary: control 0/520; treatment 0/520; 0 gains/0 losses; aggregate workSpent BYTE-IDENTICAL (123,835,203,269 both arms) -- a SECOND, DISTINCT non-participation mechanism from confirm-broad-003/004's repair-fallback saturation (ruled out by construction here: every residual row is a control-failure, so repair does not solve it). A one-off audit (scripts/stress/confirm-residual-001-archetype-audit.mjs, using the real exported extractFeatures/isMustCrossFlipperHeavy/getConfiguredAttemptConfigs functions to eliminate reimplementation drift) found 60/1200 (5.00%) of the pool genuinely archetype-eligible, 25 of which are in the residual -- a real, substantial population, not a near-zero draw. Raw-vs-mechanics-only-reduced classification matched exactly (0 mismatches across all 1200 levels). Yet all 25 eligible-and-residual rows show zero attempts of the new candidate configs; calling getConfiguredAttemptConfigs directly for one such row (J00035) confirms the config list itself correctly includes both new configs at positions 5-6, identical in shape to a working Corpus-2 case (R00817). The real solve's main loop stopped after only 4 of 6 configs on every one of the 25 rows despite MAIN_LOOP_LATE_RESERVE_CONFIG_COUNT nominally protecting the trailing 5; each row's actual nodesExpanded (~225,000,000) vastly overshoots the nominal node_budget (50,000,000) under this run's default non-strict ('legacy additive-pass') budget semantics. Working hypothesis (not yet traced to a specific stage-budget.ts line): the late-reserve guarantee does not survive this magnitude of overshoot. See reports/2026-08-26-mustcross-flipper-wide-beam-exposure-development-ab.md's 'Confirmation attempts' section. Not evidence of no mechanism -- do not promote or close negative. Do not commission a fourth cohort without first addressing the scheduling gap (e.g. --strict-total-work-budget, or a stage-budget.ts fix).

populations.reservationRationale: confirm-residual-001 found a real archetype-eligible population (25/520) but zero participation due to a scheduling gap in MAIN_LOOP_LATE_RESERVE_CONFIG_COUNT (protected the NODE-budget dimension only, not WORK). That gap is now fixed (2026-08-26, orchestration.ts's mainLoopEarlyWorkBudget/earlyGateWorkBudget). This cohort reruns the identical design against the fixed scheduler to isolate that one changed variable -- a fresh identity is required per the confirmation contract since confirm-residual-001's own residual composition already informed this candidate's diagnosis and cannot be reused.
